title: Local quasi-finiteness of schemes is etale local on the source
statement: Let $U,V,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:U\to V$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $g:V\to T$ be a morphism. If $g$ is locally quasi-finite in the scheme sense [pqf-def-quasifinite], then $g\circ p$ is locally quasi-finite. Conversely, if the underlying map of points of $p$ is surjective and $g\circ p$ is locally quasi-finite, then $g$ is locally quasi-finite. No quasi-compactness, separatedness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on these schemes or morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03X4 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-etale-local-source), including the etale-precomposition assertion in its proof; source locality means the covering equivalence of definition-property-morphisms-local-source.

proof.text: First $p$ is locally quasi-finite. At $u\in U$ choose affine opens $A\subseteq U$, $B\subseteq V$ with $u\in A$ and $p(A)\subseteq B$. By [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction], $A\to B$ is etale. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-quasi-finite] to its ring map: it is finite type and quasi-finite at every prime. These are precisely the affine witnesses at $u$ in [pqf-def-quasifinite]. This works at every $u$.
If $g$ is locally quasi-finite, apply [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-composition] to $p$ and $g$ using Step 1. This proves the forward assertion.

For the converse assume $p$ is surjective and $g\circ p$ is locally quasi-finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type], $g\circ p$ is locally of finite type. The definition [def-weil-etale-morphism] supplies flatness and local finite presentation of $p$. Hence [lem-a1-lft-flat-lfp-source-descent], applied to the triangle $U\xrightarrow{p}V\xrightarrow{g}T$, shows that $g$ is locally of finite type. This use does not require $p$ to be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 03X4, finite-type descent; Tag 02KL (lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence), locally-of-finite-type alternative, packages the same Tag 0367 affine descent and finite affine refinement for non-affine source covers.

proof.text: For the converse fix affine opens $Z\subseteq T$, $W\subseteq V$ with $g(W)\subseteq Z$. By [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction], $q:p^{-1}(W)\to W$ is etale. It is surjective: a preimage under $p$ of $w\in W$ belongs to $p^{-1}(W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens], the restriction $p^{-1}(W)\to Z$ of $g\circ p$ is locally quasi-finite. Apply [lem-a1-etale-affine-finite-fibre-refinement] to $q$ and $h=g|_W:W\to Z$. For each $z\in Z$, its conclusion writes $h^{-1}(\{z\})$ as the finite union of the images under $q$ of the finite fibres of the $A_j\to Z$. Thus $h$ has finite fibres, including the empty-$W$ case.

The restriction $g|_W:W\to Z$ is locally of finite type: [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] for $g$ from Step 3 gives the finite-type ring map for every pair of affine opens inside $W,Z$, so the reverse direction of that criterion applies to $g|_W$. Since $W,Z$ are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) also make $g|_W$ quasi-compact. It is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Now [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres], using Step 4, makes $g|_W$ quasi-finite, and [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] makes it locally quasi-finite. Take an affine open cover of $T$ and, over each member $Z$, an affine open cover by such $W$ of $g^{-1}(Z)$. Condition (3) of [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-affine-criterion] proves that $g$ is locally quasi-finite. All finiteness was used only on these affine charts, so there is no global quasi-compactness or separation requirement.
